correctness.rationale: The face excess is the sum over parts of max(0, occupancy-1). The faces with their possible doubled part i form Xi, the complete-graph one-skeleton in part i joined to the other discrete sets. Distinct Xi intersect exactly in K. The inclusion of the discrete set in its connected graph is nullhomotopic; joining the homotopy makes the inclusion of K factor up to homotopy through a contractible cone on the remaining factors. At each successive union both maps from K are thus null, the inclusions are cofibrations, and the homotopy pushout adds Xi and one suspension of K as wedge summands. The connectedness needed for this splitting holds even at r=2. A complete graph on a_i vertices has circle rank binomial(a_i-1,2), zero for a_i=2; combining its join contribution with the r-1 suspensions gives the stated integer B. For the trace, a fixed face is a union of vertex cycles. On a length-ell orbit of parts the at-most-one-per-part choices are empty or a vertex cycle of length ell, of which there are f_O. The unique doubled part must be individually fixed; inside it the pair is two fixed points or one transposition. The reduced alternating contribution of a fixed oriented simplex with k vertex cycles is (-1)^(k-1), including -1 for the empty face; hence the formula, without dividing by any 1-f_O or assuming equal sizes. In the all-size-two case each Xi is contractible, and in the exact sequence of (X,K) the relative groups identify naturally with the copies of H_(r-1)(K) indexed by the parts; their boundary is the sum. K is the boundary sphere of the cross-polytope, so its orientation character is the determinant of the signed permutation of the coordinate axes. The augmentation kernel therefore gives the claimed integral lattice, not merely the same trace. value.rationale: The first nontrivial tolerance extension of the ordinary multipartite join is a natural structured test family. A compact trace formula for the whole automorphism group resolves the missing information about part exchanges, allowing direct invariant-subspace and representation calculations beyond the known non-equivariant wedge. The all-size-two lattice also distinguishes the actual integral action from its trace. The bare wedge deduction alone would not justify acceptance.
